conventions.convention: The residue cocycle is normalized as ω(x_m,y_n)=mδ_{m,-n}B(x,y) with B a nondegenerate invariant symmetric form, and for the affine comparison B is rescaled so that a longest root has square 2, whence B(e_θ,f_θ)=1.

The untwisted central extension bracket carries the explicit central term mδ_{m,-n}B(x,y)c, and the full affine algebra adds d with [d,x_m]=mx_m, [d,c]=0 (c must be adjusted when the form is rescaled).
Affine simple-data convention α_0=δ−θ, h_0=c−θ^∨ with θ the highest root normalized to (θ,θ)=2; δ vanishes on h⊕Cc and δ(d)=1; level of a weight is its value on c.
The affine GCM is the matrix (α_j(h_i))_{0≤i,j≤ℓ} in row-coroot/column-root order, identified with the loop algebra through e_0↦f_θ⊗t, f_0↦e_θ⊗t^{−1}, h_0↦c−θ^∨ and degree-zero finite triples.

Weyl group convention s_iλ=λ−λ(h_i)α_i with dual action s_i h=h−α_i(h)h_i; the untwisted affine Weyl group is written Q^∨⋊W_0 with the coroot-lattice factor normal (the spelling W_0⋉Q^∨ denotes the same group).

Characters and products are coefficient arrays supported in a finite union of downward cones λ_j−Q^+; products, inverses and coefficient extractions are coefficientwise and no numerical value of e^λ, analytic convergence or specialization killing a denominator is asserted.

The Weyl vector is any functional with ρ(h_i)=1 for all i; it is non-unique (free complementary Cartan values) unless the simple coroots span the Cartan, and numerator and denominator acquire the same factor e^η under ρ↦ρ+η with η vanishing on all coroots.

Denominator convention P=∏_{α∈Δ^+}(1−e^{−α})^{m_α} with the actual multiplicities m_α=dim g_α (imaginary multiplicities included, simple-axis multiplicity one), D=e^ρP, and P^{−1}=Σ_{β∈Q^+}K(β)e^{−β} with K(0)=1, K=0 off Q^+.

Block induction convention: a block B of kG is induced from a block b of kH, written b^G=B, iff it is the unique block with b a split summand of Res^{G×G}_{H×H}B; otherwise b^G is left undefined, and blocks are the actual ideals kGe, not isomorphism classes.

Local block theory is set in a splitting p-modular system, defect groups are the p-subgroups D with ΔD a vertex of the residue-field block bimodule kGb, the Brauer map Br_P is coefficient projection onto C_G(P), and the Brauer correspondent is taken at an actual subgroup D, so passing to a conjugacy class loses the literal subgroup.

AC is declared exactly where used: thm-corresponding-block-bimodules-are-green-correspondents and cor-every-block-has-an-indecomposable-module-of-full-defect-vertex list def-axiom-of-choice and use it only through the finite-length Green-correspondence theorem; the First Main bijection and the block-compatibility theorem are asserted choice-free.
Evaluation modules are defined only at a≠0, with c acting as zero and with no d-action; the twisted loop definition inherits the untwisted central/degree scaling and reduces to it at r=1.

load_bearing.statement: The full untwisted affine algebra is ĝ = L̄g ⊕ Cd, with D(x_m)=mx_m, D(c)=0 and [u+ad,v+bd]=[u,v]+aD(v)−bD(u); in particular [d,x_m]=mx_m, [d,c]=0.

E is the space of formal sums Σ c_μ e^μ with support in a finite union of downward cones λ_j−Q^+, with coefficientwise addition and multiplication; inverses of 1+u (u supported in −Q^+∖{0}) are given by Σ_{k≥0}(−u)^k.
A block B of kG is induced from b, denoted b^G=B, if it is the unique block for which b | Res^{G×G}_{H×H} B (split summand); if no block or more than one block has the property, b^G is undefined.
e_0↦f_θ⊗t, f_0↦e_θ⊗t^{−1}, h_0↦c−θ^∨, together with the degree-zero assignments for the finite simple triples and the identity on ĥ, extend uniquely to an isomorphism g(Â)≅ĝ.
L̄g = Lg ⊕ Cc with bracket [u+ac,v+bc]=[u,v]_{Lg}+ω(u,v)c and [x_m,y_n]=[x,y]_{m+n}+mδ_{m,−n}B(x,y)c.

The finite root system has a unique highest root θ with θ−β∈Q_+ for every root β, long with (θ,θ)=2; α_0=δ−θ, h_0=c−θ^∨ are minimal realization data for the untwisted affine GCM Â, and [f_θ⊗t,e_θ⊗t^{−1}]=h_0.
The null root is the unique functional with δ|_{h⊕Cc}=0 and δ(d)=1; the level of a weight Λ is Λ(c), and a module generated by a weight vector of weight Λ has level Λ(c).
The unital k-algebra homomorphisms Z(kG)→k are in bijection with the primitive central block idempotents; λ_b is characterized by λ_b(b)=1 and λ_b(c)=0 for other block idempotents c.
If C_G(D) ≤ H ≤ G and b is a block of kH with defect group D, then b^G is defined; if also H ≤ N_G(D), then λ_{b^G}(z)=λ_b(Br_D(z)) for every z ∈ Z(kG).
D ch L(Λ) = Σ_{w∈W} det(w)e^{w(Λ+ρ)} and ch L(Λ) = P^{−1} Σ_{w∈W} det(w)e^{w(Λ+ρ)−ρ} for dominant integral Λ.
P=∏_{α∈Δ^+}(1−e^{−α})^{m_α} with m_α=dim g_α, and D=e^ρP; support of P lies in −Q^+ with constant coefficient one and simple-axis factor 1−e^{−α_i}.
ω(x⊗f,y⊗q)=B(x,y)Res(f′q dt) with B invariant symmetric; in particular ω(x_m,y_n)=mδ_{m,−n}B(x,y).

The roots relative to ĥ are α+nδ for finite roots α and n∈Z, and nδ for n∈Z∖{0}; the first family is real of multiplicity one with spaces g_α⊗t^n, the second imaginary of multiplicity ℓ=dim h with spaces h⊗t^n.
For a module V generated by a nonzero highest vector of weight Λ in O there are unique integers c_μ with ch V=Σ_{μ≤Λ}c_μ ch M(μ), c_Λ=1, and c_μ≠0 ⟹ (μ+ρ,μ+ρ)=(Λ+ρ,Λ+ρ).
For D ≤ G and N=N_G(D), block induction b↦b^G is a bijection from blocks of kN with defect group D to blocks of kG with defect group D, commuting with conjugation of D.
Every element is uniquely t_γw with γ∈Q^∨, w∈W_0; t_γt_η=t_{γ+η} and wt_γw^{−1}=t_{wγ}, so W_aff ≅ Q^∨⋊W_0.

concerns.concern: Step 3.1's converse ("if any block c of kN induces to B, F5 gives 1=λ_B(f)=λ_c(e)") applies the central-character formula of lem-block-induction-exists-under-centralizer-containment to a block c whose defect group is not known to be D: that lemma's formula λ_{c^G}(z)=λ_c(Br_{D_c}(z)) uses c's own defect group D_c and needs C_G(D_c)≤N, neither of which is established for an arbitrary inducing block (lem-induced-blocks-have-controlled-defect gives only D_c⊆ a conjugate of D). The uniqueness conclusion itself is standard, and the injectivity step actually used downstream (lem-first-main-theorem-injectivity) assumes both local blocks have defect group D, so this is a gap in the written argument rather than an identified false claim.

Steps 2.1 and 3.1 apply the Casimir scalar and the simple-quotient citation to simple subquotients L(μ) of V, i.e. they use the standard fact that simple objects of O are highest-weight modules; that identification is nowhere stated or cited on the page (the cited items concern Verma modules and primitive vectors only). Step 3.1's "pointwise finite defining operator" is likewise only available through the cited Casimir theorem.

Step 2.1 needs the base slices p_0=1−x and a_0=1−x. The claim about a_0 is justified in one sentence ("a reduced second letter is different from i and its reflected root has a nonzero coordinate off that axis"); the required computation, that s_iα_j=α_j−a_{ij}α_i has nonzero j-coordinate (using a_{ii}=2 and α_i independence), is not written out, and m(b)=−Σ_{j≠i}a_{ij}b_j silently uses a_{ij}≤0. The rest of the induction is explicit.

Step 1.1 cites "F1's root conventions" for the fact that the only roots on the i-th axis are ±α_i and that the α_i-factor has multiplicity one; F1 is the denominator definition, which asserts this only in passing and cites a different item. The input really used is prop-kac-moody-root-spaces-are-finite-dimensional, which does state it.

The definition body already discusses the affine normalization: it speaks of "a longest root" and asserts B(e_θ,f_θ)=1 "[o]nce the highest root θ is identified as long", while also saying no highest-root existence theorem is assumed here. Existence, uniqueness and longness of a highest root are proved later, in lem-the-affine-simple-root-alpha-zero-is-delta-minus-the-highest-root; the forward dependence inside a Definition is at minimum not stated as such.

The convention that b^G is undefined whenever more than one block of kG contains b as a restriction summand is the item's own definitional choice; it is stated clearly, but a reader coming from the Brauer-correspondence usage (where b^G is attached to the local block of kN via Br_D) may misread "more than one block" as referring to blocks of kN rather than of kG.
